articles.title: Indian PV at a turning point
articles.summary:
India’s module manufacturing capacity has expanded at remarkable speed, while domestic content requirements are pushing investment into the more complex cell manufacturing sector. Suppliers are also eyeing moves into wafer and ingot manufacturing ahead of further expansion to the domestic content rules. Activity has been more limited in polysilicon manufacturing, as with the development of facilities to produce solar glass and other bill of materials components. The challenge is no longer how much manufacturing capacity India can build, it’s whether that capacity can operate at high utilization, keep pace with fast-changing technologies and compete on cost.

articles.title: Forecasting growth
articles.summary:
India’s Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (CERC) sets the principal framework for projects connected to India’s interstate transmission system (ISTS), alongside procedures issued by the National Load Despatch Centre (NLDC), Regional Load Despatch Centres (RLDCs) and other system operators. Projects connected within a state are generally subject to the relevant State Electricity Regulatory Commission (SERC), State Load Despatch Centre (SLDC) and state grid code.

articles.title: Africa has seen oil shocks before. Why 2026 could be the turning point for clean energy
articles.summary:
Africa has been here before. Oil climbs above $100, import bills balloon, Finance ministers across the continent convene emergency sessions, and somewhere in a development bank boardroom, a clean energy investment pipeline gets quietly deprioritised while everyone waits for the price to come back down.

In 2008, the global financial crisis interrupted a Brent spike that had touched $147.
